wga:zearly/1/2mural/4callist/callist6.summary: Within a red medallion on a catacomb ceiling, a young shepherd in a belted tunic carries a sheep on his shoulders and holds a pail in his outstretched hand, with a small animal standing on either side. The simple, quickly painted figure expresses the earliest Christians' trust in Christ as the shepherd who carries his flock to safety, even through death.
facts: The pail is usually identified as a milk pail (mulctra), a pastoral attribute of the shepherd that some early Christian interpreters associated with spiritual nourishment.
The Catacomb of Callixtus on the Via Appia became the official burial ground of the 3rd-century church of Rome and contains the 'Crypt of the Popes'.
wga:zearly/1/2mural/4callist/callist6.notes: WGA gives no chamber; the specific location within the catacomb (possibly the Crypts of Lucina area) was not confirmed.
